reader.requirement: OPEN EXTEND of an indexed file (sequential access only) must position after the currently existing record with the highest prime key, so the next WRITE must exceed that key; an empty or emptied file accepts any key, and an absent OPTIONAL file is created.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehavior.FileSharingFacility by FileConnector.Edition (set from ctx.Data.DialectLevel at FileRegisterIndexed): whether another run unit may lock the file, so whether FileRegistry#MutationTarget/ConflictOnLockedRecord govern the DELETE by record locks; at 85 the facility is absent

reader.edition-search: Opened(Extend) seeds _lastWrittenPrime from the prime tree's last existing entry (_st.Edge last:true) with no edition test; grepped IndexedConnector.cs/KeyedConnector.cs for Edition|DialectBehavior (none on OPEN EXTEND).
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf21_06 covers a deleted highest record; not an empty file, a file emptied by DELETE, an absent OPTIONAL file, or the random-access refusal

probes.expected: OPEN EXTEND of an empty file accepts any first key; after reopen the highest existing key K60 bounds: equal or lower is 21, higher 00 (IX.4.9.4 GR14/GR17a); after every record is deleted EXTEND accepts A00; optional absent file: OPEN EXTEND 05 and creates it

probes.printed: COBOL2372 OPEN EXTEND 'IX' random access refused; COBOL1720 INVALID KEY on sequential-access DELETE refused; COBOL0900 the file COLLATING SEQUENCE clause requires COBOL-2002 (targeting COBOL-85)
probes.expected: EXTEND only in sequential access (§1985:IX.4.4.3 SR1); no INVALID KEY in sequential access (§1985:IX.4.3.3 SR1); the SELECT COLLATING SEQUENCE clause is not 1985 syntax

reader.notes: The highest key is read from the store at OPEN time, so deleted records do not count. Probe p4: empty file accepts K50, equal key 21, reopen bounds at K60, emptied file accepts A00, absent OPTIONAL file opens 05; p5 refuses EXTEND under random access (COBOL2372). Same output at --std 2023.

refuter.evidence: r3coll2-001, SEQUENTIAL view of the same file: OPEN EXTEND with '~' highest: 'b' (below '~' in ASCII though above 'Z') is 21; HIGH-VALUES is 00; after CLOSE and OPEN EXTEND again, '~~~' is 21 (the highest existing key is now HIGH-VALUES); sequential READ lists L S 1 A Z a T H then 10. OK §1985:IX.4.4.4 GR11.
